description:
# SSH/CLI Protocol Integration (epic)

Final epic of v3.0. Expose the simulator over real protocols so external tools can connect to mocked devices as if they were physical hardware.

## Goal

Run `cliscrape simulate` as a persistent SSH daemon backed by a state-of-the-world manifest. External automation tools (Ansible, Nornir, custom scripts) connect, run commands, and receive vendor-authentic output without touching real devices.

## Depends On

`cliscrape-quw` (simulator), `cliscrape-woo` (manifest format).

## High-Level Scope (Defer Decomposition)

* SSH server integration — `russh` is the leading candidate; evaluate alternatives when implementation begins.
* Daemon mode with configurable host keys, user auth (password + pubkey), and graceful shutdown.
* Per-connection device routing — connecting to `10.0.0.1` vs `10.0.0.2` resolves to different manifest entries.
* Validation harness — connect from a real SSH client (e.g. `paramiko` from a Python test) and assert command output matches expectations.

## Requirements

To be drawn from PROJECT.md when the simulator and manifest epics close.

## Acceptance (Epic Level)

* `cliscrape simulate --manifest m.json --listen 0.0.0.0:2222` runs as an SSH daemon.
* External SSH clients (Paramiko, OpenSSH) successfully connect, authenticate, run commands, and disconnect.
* Output matches what real-device parsing would round-trip.
* Documentation covers operator setup, key management, and security caveats (this is for testing, not production exposure).

## Risks to Flag Early

* SSH server library maturity in the Rust ecosystem evolves; pin versions deliberately.
* Vendor-specific prompt and pager behavior (`--More--` paging, escape sequences) is fiddly. Budget time for it.

## Historical Note

Originally tracked as "Phase 20" in the GSD-era roadmap.

title: Make FSM-Oracle verification strict for selected templates
description:
## Gap
The FSM-Oracle path is useful, but current verification is warning-oriented. `tests/oracle_verification.rs` describes mathematically verified and lossless behavior while intentionally allowing mismatches to pass. The tech report now downgrades this claim, but the codebase still lacks a strict oracle mode for templates we are ready to hold to that bar.

## Evidence
- Oracle tests print warnings and do not fail on mismatches.
- The tech report now describes best-effort generation plus semantic round-trip checks, not a proof system.
- Serial extraction defects show why unchecked warnings can leave bad template behavior in snapshots.

## Acceptance
- Define a selected-template allowlist for strict oracle verification, starting only with templates whose generator coverage is good enough.
- Make unexpected strict-mode mismatches fail tests or return a nonzero CLI status.
- Keep warning-only behavior available for exploratory templates, with explicit naming and docs.
- Add tests that prove strict mode fails on a known mismatch and passes for the selected allowlisted template set.
- Update docs so the oracle contract matches the actual strict versus advisory modes.

title: Semantic Mock Server (epic)
description:
# Semantic Mock Server (epic)

First epic of v3.0 (Isomorphic Ecosystem). Simulate device behavior without physical hardware or VMs.

## Goal

Provide a `cliscrape simulate` interactive shell that takes a JSON state file and synthesizes vendor-authentic CLI output for arbitrary `show` commands. Reuses the FSM-Oracle primitives (best-effort generation + round-trip checks) shipped earlier in v2.0, and leans on the Universal Ledger schemas (`cliscrape-1s8`) as the source of truth for state.

## Why This Depends on `cliscrape-1s8`

Without common schemas, the simulator would need vendor-specific JSON shapes per command. With the Universal Ledger, a single `interface` JSON record can drive `cisco_ios_show_interfaces` and `arista_eos_show_interfaces` outputs, the difference being template-driven formatting rather than data-shape divergence.

## High-Level Scope (Defer Decomposition)

This epic is intentionally not yet decomposed into child beads. Decompose when `cliscrape-1s8` closes — premature decomposition risks rework once the schema spec is concrete. Coarse work items:

* `cliscrape simulate` interactive shell scaffold (history, prompts, exit handling).
* JSON state ingestion (single device first; multi-device under `cliscrape-woo`).
* Command-to-template resolution (when user types `show version`, pick the right template; when ambiguous, prefer vendor flag from state).
* Isomorphic output synthesis using FSM-Oracle generation, validated by round-trip parse.
* Vendor-authentic formatting (column widths, banner lines, prompt strings) — preserve operational nuance.

## Requirements (from ROADMAP.md)

`MOCK-01`, `MOCK-02`.

## Acceptance (Epic Level)

* `cliscrape simulate --state state.json` enters an interactive shell.
* Typing `show version` against a fixture state synthesizes plausible output that round-trips through the same template.
* Output preserves operationally meaningful formatting for at least the templates wired in `cliscrape-1s8.2`.
* Documented user guide for authoring state files.

## Out of Scope

* Multi-device manifests (`cliscrape-woo`).
* SSH protocol integration (`cliscrape-lw0`).

## Historical Note

Originally tracked as "Phase 18" in the GSD-era roadmap.

title: State-of-the-World Manifests (epic)
description:
# State-of-the-World Manifests (epic)

Second epic of v3.0. Define the source-of-truth format for multi-device simulation state, enabling test environments that resemble realistic networks rather than single isolated devices.

## Goal

Design and implement a manifest format that maps device hostnames to commands and JSON state records, so a single artifact describes a network topology suitable for end-to-end testing.

## Depends On

`cliscrape-quw` (the simulator itself must exist before it can be orchestrated).

## High-Level Scope (Defer Decomposition)

* Manifest schema design — JSON or YAML; pick what composes well with the Universal Ledger schemas. A manifest references states; states use the Universal Ledger vocabulary.
* Hostname-to-state resolution. The simulator picks state from the manifest based on which device a connection is targeting.
* Variant selection. A manifest may declare multiple state variants (`baseline`, `incident`, `post-recovery`) for the same hostname.
* Example manifests under `examples/manifests/` covering single-device, two-device, and a small spine-leaf topology.

## Requirements

To be drawn from PROJECT.md when `cliscrape-quw` closes; current roadmap entry has placeholder requirements.

## Acceptance (Epic Level)

* Manifest format specified and documented.
* The simulator (`cliscrape-quw`) accepts `--manifest` and resolves device state correctly.
* At least three example manifests committed and exercised by integration tests.

## Out of Scope

* SSH wire protocol (`cliscrape-lw0`).

## Historical Note

Originally tracked as "Phase 19" in the GSD-era roadmap.
